cause: Scans the entire keyspace sequentially in O(N) time, blocking all client connections on the single-threaded event loop.
fix: Replace with the non-blocking cursor-based SCAN command: SCAN 0 MATCH <pattern> COUNT 100

cause: Returns all fields and values of a hash in O(N) time. Large hashes consume massive network bandwidth and block reactor serialization.
fix: Paginate large hashes using HSCAN, or fetch only required fields with HMGET / HGET.

cause: Fetches all members of a set in O(N) time. When sets grow past thousands of members, this causes noticeable latency spikes.
fix: Paginate set members iteratively using SSCAN, or check specific membership with SISMEMBER / SMISMEMBER.

cause: Traversing large lists from start to end in O(S+N) time causes high memory allocation and CPU overhead.
fix: Paginate with smaller index windows (e.g. LRANGE key 0 49) or trim lists regularly with LTRIM.

cause: Sorts collection elements in memory with O(N+M*log(M)) complexity, which is heavily CPU-bound.
fix: Pre-sort data on insertion into a Sorted Set (ZSET) and query instantaneously with ZRANGE.

cause: Computes set intersections, unions, or differences on the server over large collections, consuming significant CPU.
fix: Cache results using SUNIONSTORE / SINTERSTORE, or compute unions in application memory.

cause: Synchronous deletion of large collections (hashes/sets/lists with > 10,000 items) blocks the main thread during jemalloc deallocation.
fix: Use UNLINK to deallocate memory asynchronously in background IO worker threads.

cause: Synchronously frees all keys in memory, causing a multi-second latency freeze on large databases.
fix: Always use asynchronous flushing: FLUSHALL ASYNC or FLUSHDB ASYNC.

cause: Batching hundreds of keys in a single multi-key command creates large payload packets and serialization delays.
fix: Chunk multi-key commands into smaller batches of 50 to 100 keys.
